_comment: Hardware: qrb5165_flowc -- QRB5165 v66 through Flow C: HTA (CPU_P) + Hexagon v66 DSP (CPU_E) + Kryo 585 CPU (CPU_X), one lane each. Profiles are the tile-level results.csv files flowc/artifacts.py writes from measurements/qrb5165_v66.json.

Periodic taskset -- each model runs at its OWN period, drawn from the model bank's period_ms and snapped to a multiple of the fastest task's (3 ms) so the hyperperiod is just the slowest period (15 ms):
mlp_control: period 3 ms (333.3 Hz), 1 copy(ies), 0.107 ms each (serial on CPU, 1 dispatches), 3.6% of a core, 15 instances over the horizon
mlp_control: window 2 ms (drawn from window_ms 2-8 ms, then fitted to the period; deadline = 13.08x measured runtime), start_time 0 ms
dronet: period 15 ms (66.7 Hz), 1 copy(ies), 0.645 ms each (serial on DSP, 1 dispatches), 4.3% of a core, 3 instances over the horizon
dronet: window 11 ms (drawn from window_ms 5-20 ms, then fitted to the period; deadline = 17.05x measured runtime), start_time 0 ms
Peak backend utilization of the periodic set: 0.04 (budget 0.75) -- CPU 0.04/1, DSP 0.04/1, HTA 0.00/1.
Horizon 45 ms = 3.0 x hyperperiod; num_instances is ceil(horizon / period) per network, 26 operations in total.

Sporadic tasks placed in the gaps with non-overlapping windows, no edges to the periodic taskset (an edge across the boundary fans out to every periodic instance): yolov8n_a [5, 63] ms, yolov8n_b [65, 174] ms, yolov8n_c [283, 387] ms, yolov8n_d [470, 599] ms.

Edges chain the copies of one model, which share its period; models at different rates get none, because workload_factory pairs periodic instances by index and that only means something at equal periods.
No p_core_speedup: it scales only the synthetic-timing fallback, so applying it on top of profiled CSVs would fabricate timings.
dronet: Steering CNN, 1 tile, composes on all three lanes (hta 2.03 ms / dsp 0.645 / cpu 7.00). The baseline arm's mid-size periodic slot.

mlp_control: Control policy, 1 tile. CPU cell is the fp32 context (107.3 us): QnnCpu's int8 path returns a constant for this network regardless of input (measurements/qrb5165_v66.json, _correctness_note in bindings/mlp_control.json). HTA is capability-excluded (elu_s8), so its profile row carries the derived exclusion cost.

yolov8n: 640x640 ultralytics export, backbone + head (2 tiles), ~28.6 ms serial on the DSP. The head is capability-excluded on HTA (Transpose), so its HTA profile row carries the derived exclusion cost. NOT the FPGA bank's 64x64 yolov8_nano -- no cross-target latency comparison is valid.
